subject: Production latency spikes — SLA & renewal discussion
messages:
From: Lucy Cheng <lucy@quantisys.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spikes — SLA & renewal discussion

Hi Dylan,

We’ve seen repeated latency spikes in our production inference pipeline over the past two weeks. p95 and p99 tail latency regularly crosses our acceptable threshold, and two customer-facing microservices dropped requests at peak times on Jan 9 and Jan 12. This is a blocker as we approach our renewal window — we need clearer uptime and latency commitments (and an escalation path) before we can proceed with an expansion.

I’ve attached a short incident summary (incident_summary_Q1.pdf). Can we set up a call this week to discuss a premium SLA or dedicated capacity options and what credits/remediation we would expect if similar incidents recur?

Thanks,
Lucy Cheng
Head of Platform, Quantisys
lucy@quantisys.com

Attachment: incident_summary_Q1.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Cheng <lucy@quantisys.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes — SLA & renewal discussion

Thanks for the detail, Lucy — I’m really sorry Quantisys has been impacted. We take tail latency seriously. I’ve looped in Neha (sales engineering) and Marissa (CS) so we can triage and put a remediation/offer on the table quickly.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Quick sync (30 min) this week to review the incident summary and traffic patterns — can you do Tue or Wed?
- We’ll run a focused analysis on your recent workload and propose either a dedicated pool configuration or a Premium SLA package with explicit p99 targets.
- If desired, we can provision a 30-day Premium trial while we finalize terms.

Please share any metrics dashboards or the logs folder (Drive link acceptable) so Neha can start profiling.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production latency spikes — SLA & renewal discussion (analysis notes)

Internal notes — quick profile after pulling the logs Lucy shared:
- Pattern: spikes align with bursty batch jobs from Quantisys between 02:00–03:00 UTC (large prompt sizes, longer sequences).
- Root cause candidates: suboptimal batching/batch timeouts at their client side + hotspotting on a shared hosted pool (KV cache thrash).

Options to present:
1) Premium SLA (hosted) — guaranteed 99.95% availability, p99 inference latency target <= 220ms for requests <= 512 tokens; includes priority routing, dedicated cache lanes, and 24/7 on-call escalations. Estimated uplift: +35% cost over current tier.
2) Dedicated pool — customer-dedicated GPU pool with autoscale and pinned capacity; stronger isolation and predictable tail performance. Pricing: higher OPEX but lower variability at p99; commit discounts available if they sign 12 months.
3) Short remediation plan during renewal: 30-day Premium trial + engineering playbook (KV tuning, client-side backoff) — gives us data before a 12-month commit.

Recommendation: propose the 30-day Premium trial + explicit SLA doc and an optional conversion to Dedicated with a 12-month commit at a 15% discount. I’ll draft numbers if we agree.

-Neha
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Cheng <lucy@quantisys.com>, Mark Rivera <mark@quantisys.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Premium SLA trial & conversion path — Quantisys

Hi Lucy / Mark,

Thanks for the call last week. Per our discussion, attached is a concise proposal and the draft Premium SLA for your review (redwood_premium_sla.pdf; quantisys_proposal_v1.docx). Highlights:
- 30-day complimentary Premium trial (activated within 7 days of signed acceptance)
- Target SLA during trial: 99.90% availability; if converted to paid Premium/Dedicated the target will be 99.95% with p99 latency target <= 220ms for requests <=512 tokens
- Compensation: during the trial period, we’ll credit service-impacting incidents at 5x the prorated trial fee; once on paid Premium/Dedicated, service credit terms per the SLA apply (we propose 10% monthly credit for a single monthly miss, capped at 50% per month).
- Conversion pricing: 12-month commit to Dedicated => 15% off list; Premium hosted SLA => +35% over current plan.

Action items for Quantisys: review SLA PDF and the proposal doc, confirm whether you want the trial provisioned in us-west or eu-west (we can enable eu-west but billing/contracting needs to reflect region). I’ve included a DocuSign link for an acceptance stub if you want to expedite.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_premium_sla.pdf, quantisys_proposal_v1.docx
Related link: https://docusign.net/Sign/quantisys-premium-offer
From: Mark Rivera <mark@quantisys.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lucy Cheng <lucy@quantisys.com>
Cc: procurement@quantisys.com, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Premium SLA trial & conversion path — Quantisys

Marissa — thanks for the clear proposal. A few follow-ups from our side before committing:
1) p99 definition: is this measured at our account level after routing (client-observed) or at the host runtime? We need client-observed p99 to reflect end-to-end experience.
2) The trial compensation math (5x prorated) feels light given recent impact. Can we discuss a higher credit or a one-time goodwill credit if we see another SLA-triggering incident during the trial?
3) EU region: we want eu-west for production traffic (GDPR + latency to our EU customers). If you enable eu-west for the trial, will the same latency targets and credits apply? If not, we’ll need a separate SLA clause.

Procurement also asked for a rough number on price delta for a 12-month commit to Dedicated (ballpark USD/month) to run through internal budget approval.

Can we get answers to the above and a revised DocuSign with a stronger trial-credit option?

Thanks,
Mark Rivera
VP Engineering, Quantisys
mark@quantisys.com
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Mark Rivera <mark@quantisys.com>, Lucy Cheng <lucy@quantisys.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Premium SLA trial & conversion path — Quantisys (finalized offer)

Mark / Lucy — thanks for the thoughtful questions; below are clear answers and a final offer so your procurement/legal can review.

1) p99 measurement: we will report both host-runtime and client-observed p99. The contractual SLA will reference client-observed p99 measured at the account ingress (post-routing) to reflect end-to-end latency. We’ll include the exact measurement window and sampling method in the SLA appendix.

2) Trial compensation: we’ll update the trial acceptance to include a one-time goodwill credit equal to 25% of one month’s estimated Premium fees if Quantisys experiences any SLA-qualifying incident during the 30-day trial. Additionally, trial-impacting incidents will trigger incident reviews and prioritized remediation.

3) EU region: we can provision the 30-day trial in eu-west with identical latency targets; if you convert to paid Dedicated in eu-west, pricing will include cross-region capacity costs — we’ll provide a region-specific appendix.

4) Ballpark pricing: Dedicated 12-month commit (equivalent capacity to your current footprint + 20% headroom) — estimated USD 82,500/month list; with a 12-month commit we can offer 15% discount => ~USD 70,125/month. Premium hosted SLA is roughly 35% uplift over your current plan; we’ll attach a line-item breakdown to the HubSpot deal.

Next steps:
- I’ll circulate an updated SLA PDF and DocuSign with the goodwill trial credit and measurement appendix by EOD Tue.
- If that looks good, sign the acceptance stub to activate the trial (you can choose eu-west or us-west).

HubSpot deal: https://hub.redwood.com/deals/QSYS-2026-01

Appreciate the partnership here — we want to ensure you’re comfortable with the reliability guarantees before you expand.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132
